name: footprints
meaning: Paglya means footprint. The footprint is a sign of arrival and makes way for gods, goddesses, ancestors and guests. It is also called the feet of Lakshmi-Vishnu.
context: Diwali. Drawn as a pair at the threshold, then one foot ahead of the other, from the entrance stairs to the place of Lakshmi Puja.

name: four-petalled lotus
meaning: The lotus is the motif drawn most often in Mandana. The design spreads out on the petals, which stands for the expansion of the universe.
context: Drawn with traditional colours and ringed with smaller motifs; also used to decorate the chariot of Lakshmi at Diwali.

name: eight-petalled lotus
meaning: Lakshmi is believed to reside over the lotus. Four- and eight-petalled lotuses are the ones seen most often.
context: Makar Sankranti, Dev Shayani and Dev Uthani Gyaras, and Holi. Drawn in the house, courtyard or temple area, in small or large sizes.

name: six-petalled flower
meaning: A six-petalled flower suggests the lotus-shaped throne of the goddess Lakshmi.
context: Part of the floral repertoire of four to eight petals drawn on floors in Rajasthan, for example in the Bundi region.

name: chariot of Lakshmi
meaning: Lakshmi is believed to reside in this Mandana. It has sixteen square sections, each holding a lit earthen lamp.
context: Drawn at the place of Lakshmi Puja on the no-moon night of Diwali, with a four-petalled lotus and an eight-petalled lotus nearby.

name: threshold band
meaning: Drawn to invite and welcome the gods, bring good fortune into the house and drive away difficulties. It is mostly triangular.
context: Made in every house at Diwali, inside the main entrance. Its place is fixed and it is not drawn anywhere else.

name: swastika
meaning: The swastika is drawn in many designs because it is held to be auspicious in itself. The Sanskrit word comes from su (good) and asti (being).
context: Many rituals and ceremonies begin and end with drawing a swastika in rice flour or turmeric paste; a swastika Mandana is drawn for Diwali in the Jodhpur region.

name: hand fan
meaning: The beejani is a hand fan. It was used in courts, royal houses and religious ceremonies to fan the deities.
context: One of the everyday objects in the Mandana repertoire. Meena women also make the fans themselves.

name: chaupad square
meaning: Chaupad is a cross-shaped board game; the word means four arms, after the playing surface.
context: One of the everyday objects drawn as a chowk on the floor in Rajasthan.

name: stepwell square
meaning: The stepwell pattern shows a baori, a well with symmetrical steps leading down to the water, like an inverted fortress.
context: Drawn as a chowk on the floor in Rajasthan, where stepwells such as Chand Baori stand.

name: peacock
meaning: The peacock belongs to the protective bestiary painted on house walls at Diwali.
context: A popular wall design in Bundi, usually painted in pairs flanking a central flower on gables or walls.

name: sun
meaning: Sun and moon motifs stand for balance, continuity and the passing of time.
context: Drawn among the celestial motifs on walls and floors.

name: moon
meaning: Sun and moon motifs stand for balance, continuity and the passing of time.
context: Drawn among the celestial motifs on walls and floors.

name: Lakshmi's feet with sun and moon
meaning: A square holds a pair of stylised feet of the goddess Lakshmi, crowned by the sun and the moon.
context: Drawn by the women of one family on a freshly plastered courtyard near Jodhpur while preparing for Diwali.
